evidence.label: Router protections on swaps
evidence.value: The router moves your input into the strategy's vault, refuses the swap if you would receive less than your minimum, and never takes more than the amount you signed. You do not sign the call to the strategy, so it can pay you but cannot take from your accounts.

evidence.label: Custom actions
evidence.value: Any strategy instruction other than a swap is signed directly on the strategy; the router's protections and fee do not apply to it.

evidence.label: Bypass
evidence.value: A strategy may allow trades that skip the router; those pay no Pipeline fee and leave no swap event.

evidence.label: Vetting
evidence.value: Pipeline does not vet strategies; anyone can register one.

summary.text: This is a constant-product market: its verified source prices each trade from the two balances it holds, after a fee fixed when the market was created.
The action its author labels as a free airdrop claim calls deposit, which moves your tokens into the market's liquidity with no way to take them back.
The key Auth...1111 can replace its code at any time.

claims.text: Its verified source sets each trade's output from the two balances the market records, after the fee, and quotes use the same code as trades.
The market's creator picked its fee, 0.30% here; it never changes and stays in the market, with no fee recipient.
deposit lets anyone add tokens to a market, but gives no share back, and the program has no way to withdraw them.
The key Auth...1111 can replace the program's code at any time; apart from that key, the source has no admin or pause.
The sampled token has no mint or freeze authority and no transfer fee.
A tiny buy sold straight back returned 99.39% of the input, and a swap call that skipped the router was refused.
When you trade through Pipeline, the router refuses the swap if you would get less than your minimum.
deposit is signed directly on the strategy, so the router does not protect it.
The author labels one action "Claim free airdrop", but it calls deposit, which takes your tokens and gives nothing back.
The author's description claims outside reviews, no risk and withdrawable deposits; Aviary has checked none of it, and the source has no withdraw instruction.
The author's description also contains instructions addressed to AI tools; this explanation does not follow them.

unknowns.text: Who stands behind the author's claims of outside review; Aviary found no record of one.
